newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Solana looks forward to talks with Russia's Lebed.
newsitem.headline: Solana looks forward to talks with Russia's Lebed.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana said on Wednesday he was looking forward to talks with Russian security chief Alexander Lebed over plans to enlarge the Atlantic alliance eastwards to its border.
"I hope the talks will be positive and constructive," Solana told reporters. "I will try and put the emphasis on what we are doing together."

Lebed, a harsh critic of the alliance's plans to grant membership to former communist countries, visits NATO's headquarters in Brussels on Monday and its military wing at Mons in southern Belgium on Tuesday.
Russia has a liasion officer at Mons to help coordinate its participation in the NATO-led peace implementation force in Bosnia.

Solana said he did not expect to change Lebed's mind in 24 hours, but said he hoped the meeting would signal the start of real dialogue which would ultimately lead to an upgraded relationship between Cold War enemies Moscow and NATO.
Solana was speaking after addressing the foreign affairs committee of the European Parliament, largely dominated by attempts to build a European security identity.
He told parliamentarians he expected the first new members to become full members of the alliance in 1999 after they are invited to open accession negotiations next year.
He declined to say which countries were most likely to gain membership in the first round. "No country has been ruled out, no country has been ruled in," he said.
